curriculum.title: God Made and Cares: Family Prayer and Service Flex

core.big_idea: A flexible unit may reinforce the cycle through a family prayer, service, or generosity practice.

passages.reading_note: Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.
Read in context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Optional prayer and service flex with a safe default biblical anchor.

claims.statement: Jesus gives His disciples a pattern of prayer centred on God, daily needs, forgiveness, and help.
Christians are called to serve one another through love.
A family prayer or service flex may reinforce the cycle by practising prayer and loving service without making the practice a measure of spiritual worth.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The underlying biblical or curriculum principle is distinguishable from the specific modern implementation, which requires contextual wisdom rather than a direct one-to-one command.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present the chosen modern implementation as the only biblically faithful option unless the evidence actually requires it.

core.interpretation_skill: Concrete language; identify prayer or song; locate in the big story

learning.foundation_objective: Retell the main action in To be selected by curriculum editor and state in simple language that a flexible unit may reinforce the cycle through a family prayer, service, or generosity practice.
learning.extension_objective: Place this event in the Bible's big story and name one concrete way to trust, thank, obey, or care for others in response.
know: The principal passage or required editor selection is Matthew 6:9-13.
A flexible unit may reinforce the cycle through a family prayer, service, or generosity practice.
The lesson belongs within the wider Cycle 1 structure.
understand: Meaning depends on immediate context, genre, and the evidence actually available.
Direct textual observation should remain distinguishable from synthesis, inference, framework design, prudential judgment, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before giving an interpretation.

become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage or synthesis.
Student can support the big idea with the appropriate evidence class.

activities.title: Prayer and Service Plan
steps: Read the selected evidence and record direct observations.
Place observations, interpretations, framework choices, or prudential applications into the resource categories.
Discuss which conclusions require more than direct textual wording.
Write one careful response that follows from the evidence.
activities.learning_link: Makes the lesson’s evidence classification and formation aim visible.

activities.title: Evidence Class Check
steps: Read several statements connected to the lesson.
Classify each as text observation, synthesis, framework choice, prudential judgment, or application.
Return to the evidence and justify each classification.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Use verbal responses instead of written cards.

family.title: God Made and Cares: Family Prayer and Service Flex
family.parent_intro: Start with the selected passage. For a flex template, do not use the lesson until the editor has selected and reviewed the passage.

flow.instructions: Connect this lesson to something already learned in Cycle 1.
Read selected portions of Matthew 6:9-13 and name direct observations. If this is a flex template, the editor must replace the placeholder with the approved passage before publication.

Use the Prayer and Service Plan resource verbally, on paper, or with the provided worksheet.
Choose one simple act of service you can do together and one short prayer to pray before or after it.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before using theological or curriculum shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read the passage aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe where helpful.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, giving amounts, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, giving, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the selected evidence, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
